numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Before the fix, array_equivalent on native complex arrays viewed the data as float pairs and compared real and imaginary parts independently; e.g. array_equivalent(np.array([1+nanj]), np.array([2+nanj])) returned False with dtype_equal=True, while dtype_equal=False returned True, and Series.equals returned False.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: A complex value is NA if either its real or imaginary part is NaN, so both elements are NA and should be equivalent: array_equivalent(np.array([1+nanj]), np.array([2+nanj])) should return True, and Series.equals should return True.
trigger_conditions: elements containing NaN in either the real or imaginary part
non-NaN parts differ between the two arrays

input_output_examples.input: Series.equals on the same complex elements with NaN imaginary part and differing real parts

oracle_clues: dtype_equal=False path is the reference: it uses (left == right) | (np.isnan(left) & np.isnan(right)) and must agree with the dtype_equal=True path
3.0.x used np.isnan on the complex array and returned True for this case

numerical_characteristics.dtype: native complex128 (c16) and complex64 (c8), plus big-endian >c16 and >c8 as exercised by the tests; float16 and longdouble also take the numpy fallback path
category_specific_evidence: A complex value is NA if either its real or imaginary part is NaN; the fix compares whole elements using np.isnan on the complex array.

The old fastpath viewed native complex arrays as float pairs and compared real and imaginary parts independently, which gave the wrong answer for elements that are both NA but differ in their non-NaN part.

Reported example: array_equivalent(np.array([1+nanj]), np.array([2+nanj])) returned False with dtype_equal=True but True with dtype_equal=False; Series.equals returned False where it should return True; 3.0.x returned True.
Correct handling is the numpy comparison ((left == right) | (np.isnan(left) & np.isnan(right))).all(), which matches the dtype_equal=False path.

New test test_array_equivalent_complex_nan_component is parametrized over dtype in [c16, c8, >c16, >c8] and dtype_equal in [True, False]. It checks NaN in the imaginary part, NaN in the real part, a mixed array with an equal finite element and a shared NA element, and a case with differing finite elements that must not be equivalent.
Related regression fixes GH-65192 (float16, byte-swapped) and GH-66160 (complex NaN) are unreleased in 3.1.0.dev.
reproduction_risks: Byte-swapped complex viewed as float pairs can silently reinterpret bytes (GH#65192), so non-native dtypes must not reach the view path.
